subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept this internal yielding glob walker and bootstrap-hook scheduling as the bounded fix for bootstrap-context event-loop stalls despite possible prompt-ordering and session-interleaving changes?
rationale: The patch has strong evidence and no concrete blocking defect, but bootstrap files and hook ordering directly shape agent/session context, so automation cannot safely accept the upgrade behavior on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Land After Exact-Head Verification
options.body: Accept the bounded scheduling and glob-resolution tradeoff, rebase onto current main, rerun exact-head checks and focused runtime proof, then merge.

options.title: Require Live Channel Proof
options.body: Keep the implementation but require a current-head embedded-run with active channel traffic demonstrating that channel I/O remains responsive during bootstrap.

options.title: Pause For Broader Isolation
options.body: Hold or close this branch if maintainers prefer worker isolation or another shared filesystem scheduling design over a custom bootstrap walker.

recommendation.title: Land After Exact-Head Verification
recommendation.body: Accept the bounded scheduling and glob-resolution tradeoff, rebase onto current main, rerun exact-head checks and focused runtime proof, then merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest merged history across internal hooks, bootstrap hooks, and boundary-safe workspace reads.
